first_diff_lines: -1. **Structure matters more than parameter precision.** Adding a temperature-dependent ethanol limit P_max(T) cuts the training chi-square from 3675 (Level 1 baseline) to 1683 (M2, one extra parameter); also estimating the inhibition exponent (M5) gives 1116 (reduced chi-square 12.6 → 3.9). By the rule fixed in advance (D-24) **M5 is preferred**. It still does not fit within the stated noise, and it **fails badly when the only 37 C run is left out** (leave-one-run-out chi-square per point 1629), so its 37 C behaviour rests on R8 alone.

-2. **The linear ethanol-inhibition form (n = 1) used in Level 1 is not supported**: fixing n = 3 instead lowers the baseline chi-square by 875; M5 estimates n = 2.43 (profile 95% [2.00, 3.12]). **P_max and n are not separable** (linearised correlation +0.98, a ridge); only their combination is determined, and P_max = 195 g/L lies well above any ethanol observed (maximum 107.8 g/L).
